BEFORE THE NEW MEXICO PUBLIC REGULATION COMMISSION


IN THE MATTER OF SOUTHWESTERN
PUBLIC SERVICE COMPANY’S
APPLICATION FOR: (1) REVISION OF
ITS RETAIL RATES UNDER ADVICE
NOTICE 341; AND (2) OTHER                                Case No. 25-00079-UT
ASSOCIATED RELIEF

SOUTHWESTERN PUBLIC SERVICE
COMPANY,

APPLICANT




            STIPULATION TESTIMONY OF ALEX EUBANKS

                              On behalf of
                 Coalition for Clean Affordable Energy


                             July 2, 2026

I.     INTRODUCTION AND QUALIFICATIONS ................................................................................ 1

                                                                       i
  1                        I.     INTRODUCTION AND QUALIFICATIONS

 2   Q. Please state your name, position, and business address.

 3   A. My name is Alex Eubanks. I am the New Mexico Representative for the Southwest Energy

 4   Efficiency Project, or SWEEP. My business address is 2334 Broadway, Suite A, Boulder, Colorado

 5   80304. I am based in Albuquerque, New Mexico.

 6   Q. On whose behalf are you testifying in this proceeding?

 7   A. I am testifying on behalf of the Coalition for Clean Affordable Energy, or CCAE.

 8   Q. Are you the same Alex Eubanks who previously filed Direct Testimony in this

 9   proceeding on behalf of CCAE?

10   A. Yes.

11   Q. Have you completed any utility regulatory or ratemaking training relevant to your work

12   since filing your Direct Testimony?

13   A. Yes. I completed the Spring 2026 National Association of Regulatory Utility Commissioners

14   Rate School, which covered utility regulation, ratemaking principles, rate design, cost allocation,

15   revenue requirements, and program evaluation. That training is relevant to my work evaluating

16   utility program design, policy implementation, and customer impacts of the EAP.



17                      II.     PURPOSE AND SUMMARY OF TESTIMONY

18   Q. What is the purpose of your testimony?

19   A. The purpose of my testimony is to support approval of the Comprehensive Stipulation filed

20   with the New Mexico Public Regulation Commission (“Commission”) on June 22, 2026,

21   consistent with CCAE’s position in Section 2.5 of the Stipulation.


                                                      1
  1   My testimony focuses on Section 1.12 of the Stipulation, which addresses Southwestern Public

 2   Service Company’s proposed Electric Affordability Program (“EAP”). Specifically, I explain

 3   how the EAP terms in Section 1.12 reasonably resolve, or create a process to resolve, the EAP

 4   issues I raised in my Direct Testimony.

 5   Q. Is there a specific section of the Stipulation that is the focus of your testimony?

 6   A. Yes, my testimony focuses on terms in Section 1.12, the Electric Affordability Program.

 7   Q. Has Staff opposed the EAP provisions in Section 1.12?

 8   A. No. Staff opposes the Stipulation on other issues, but Staff’s Statement in Opposition states

 9   that Staff does not oppose Section 1.12, the Electric Affordability Program provision.

10   Q. What are the terms of Section 1.12 that you testify about?

11   A. Section 1.12 includes four EAP terms that I address in this testimony:

12   (a) SPS shall update its affordability and budget analysis and evaluate whether the

13   $750,000 annual budget is sufficient under current proposed rates. SPS shall

14   provide the analysis in its next base rate case;

15   (b) SPS shall make a one-time shareholder contribution of $750,000 to improve

16   program reach, supplement benefits, or support outreach and administration;

17   (c) SPS shall convene an EAP collaborative working group within 60 days after

18   approval of this Stipulation to evaluate implementation, data, reporting, eligibility,

19   budget sufficiency, cost recovery, and future modifications. Recommendations

20   from the working group will be included in SPS’s next base rate case; and,

21   (d) SPS shall coordinate EAP implementation with other low-income programs,

22   including energy efficiency, weatherization, LIHEAP, and customer outreach

23   resources.



                                                        2
  1   Q. Does New Mexico law authorize the Commission to approve low-income affordability

 2   programs like the EAP?

 3   A. I am not offering a legal opinion. However, I understand that SPS proposes the EAP under

 4   NMSA 1978, Section 62-8-6, as amended in 2025, which allows the Commission to approve

 5   rates and programs designed to reduce the burden of energy costs on low-income customers.

 6   That statutory framework is consistent with the purpose of the EAP and with the

 7   recommendations I made in my Direct Testimony.

 8   Q. Are the terms of the Stipulation similar to recommendations you made in your Direct

 9   Testimony?

10   A. Yes. Section 1.12 reflects several of the primary recommendations I made in my Direct

11   Testimony. My Direct Testimony recommended that the Commission approve the EAP with

12   modifications related to program reach and budget support, cost recovery, shareholder funding, a

13   collaborative working group, and coordination with energy efficiency, weatherization, and

14   customer outreach programs.

15   Section 1.12 addresses those recommendations by requiring SPS to update its affordability and

16   budget analysis, make a one-time $750,000 shareholder contribution, convene an EAP

17   collaborative working group, and coordinate EAP implementation with other low-income

18   programs, including energy efficiency, weatherization, LIHEAP, and customer outreach

19   resources. While Section 1.12 does not adopt every recommendation exactly as I proposed, it

20   provides a reasonable settlement framework for approving the EAP now and evaluating future

21   improvements through the working group and SPS’s next base rate case.

22   In particular, the Stipulation does not adopt my recommendation to recover EAP costs through a

23   volumetric energy-charge mechanism at this time. However, Section 1.12 requires the EAP



                                                    3
  1   working group to evaluate cost recovery and future modifications. In my opinion, that is a

 2   reasonable settlement resolution because it preserves cost recovery for further review after SPS

 3   and stakeholders have implementation data from the program.



 4              III.     SPS'S PROPOSED ELECTRIC AFFORDABILITY PROGRAM

 5   Q. Please summarize SPS's proposed Electric Affordability Program.

 6   A. SPS proposes to establish Rate No. 89, the Electric Affordability Program Rider, or EAP. The

 7   proposed EAP would be available to residential customers in SPS's New Mexico service territory

 8   who are qualified for and receive LIHEAP assistance during the applicable federal fiscal year.

 9   To be considered a Qualified Customer under the rider, the customer must also agree to be

10   placed on SPS's Average Monthly Payment Plan, or AMPP, and must agree to a payment

11   schedule. That payment schedule would require the customer to pay the current monthly bill

12   after the application of the Affordability bill credit and, if applicable, to pay a portion of the

13   customer’s pre-EAP arrears. 1

14   The proposed program has two components: an Affordability Component and an Arrearage

15   Forgiveness Component. 2

16   Q. How would the Affordability Component work?

17   A. The Affordability Component would provide a bill credit to qualifying customers. The filed

18   rider states that the credit would be calculated as one-twelfth of the difference between SPS's

19   estimate of the Qualified Customer's annual electric bill and three percent of 150 percent of the

20   Department of Health and Human Services Poverty Guidelines for a household of four. 3

  1   SPS proposes to provide supplemental assistance to Residential Service customers during June,

 2   July, August, and September. For Residential Space Heating customers, SPS proposes to provide

 3   supplemental assistance during November, December, January, and February. 4

 4   The filed rider also states that LIHEAP benefits would not be considered in calculating the EAP

 5   credit. Instead, any LIHEAP benefit would be applied to the portion of the customer's full annual

 6   bill that exceeds the customer's affordable percentage-of-income payment, and any remaining

 7   LIHEAP benefit would be applied to arrears. 5

 8   Q. How would the Arrearage Forgiveness Component work?

 9   A. Under the filed rider, a monthly arrearage credit would be applied after SPS receives the

10   Qualified Customer's payment. The rider states that payments under the Arrearage Forgiveness

11   Component shall not exceed one percent of the customer's annual income. The credit would be

12   designed to retire pre-EAP arrears over twelve months for Qualified Customers with arrears of

13   $200 or less. For Qualified Customers with arrears greater than $200, the credit would be

14   designed to retire arrears over twenty-four months. 6

15   Q. How would customers enroll in the EAP?

16   A. The filed rider states that there is no specific enrollment period. Qualified Customers would

17   be auto-enrolled when SPS is notified that the customer has enrolled in LIHEAP. However, the

18   rider also states that enrollment participation is limited to a first-come, first-served basis. 7

19   In my opinion, that first-come, first-served limitation makes the proposed budget, expected

20   participation, and reporting requirements especially important. If the program budget is limited,

 2   quickly the budget may be exhausted, and what happens when otherwise eligible customers seek

 3   assistance after the budget has been fully committed.

 4   Q. How does SPS propose to fund the EAP?

 5   A. SPS proposes to recover EAP costs through a line-item charge on all rate schedules. The

 6   proposed monthly charges include $0.35 per month for Residential Service customers, $0.35 per

 7   month for Residential Space Heating customers, $0.35 per month for Small General Service

 8   customers, $0.63 per month for Secondary General customers, $1.39 per month for Primary

 9   General customers, and $137.84 per month for Large General Service-Transmission customers at

10   both 69 kV and 115 kV and above. 8

11   SPS also proposes to establish an EAP Tracker Account to compare amounts recovered to actual

12   program expenditures. The filed rider states that the EAP Tracker Account balance would be

13   provided to the Commission annually and that SPS may petition the Commission to adjust the

14   EAP Rider to address the tracker balance. 9

15   Q. What is SPS's proposed initial program budget?

16   A. SPS proposes an initial annual EAP budget of $750,000. SPS states in response to Staff that it

17   did not perform a new analysis regarding the budget since its last base rate case, Case No. 22-

18   00286-UT. SPS further states that the $750,000 budget was described by SPS witness Brooke

19   Trammell in that prior case. 10

20   Q. What does SPS estimate regarding expected participation and benefit levels?

21   A. In response to CCAE, SPS states that approximately 2,800 customers are expected to be

 2   customers are expected to be Residential customers and 28 percent are expected to be Residential

 4   SPS also provides estimated benefit amounts. For Residential customers, SPS states that the

 5   average EAP monthly credit could be $67 and the median monthly credit may be $52. For

 6   Residential Space Heating customers, SPS states that the average EAP monthly credit could be

 7   $68 and the median monthly credit may be $53. SPS states that the average annual EAP credit is

 8   $268 for Residential customers and $272 for Residential Space Heating customers. 12

 9   Q. Does SPS expect the EAP to reach all LIHEAP customers in its New Mexico service

10   territory?

11   A. No. SPS states that it expects the bill credits to benefit approximately 2,800 LIHEAP

12   customers, or approximately 50 percent of the total LIHEAP customer population in SPS

13   territory. SPS also states that not all LIHEAP customers have an average bill high enough to

14   meet the eligibility requirements. 13

15   Q. Does the shareholder contribution address concerns about program reach and budget

16   sufficiency?

17   A. Yes, in part. SPS stated in discovery that it expects affordability assistance bill credits to

18   benefit approximately 2,800 LIHEAP customers, or approximately 50 percent of the total

19   LIHEAP customer population in SPS territory, and that SPS is unable to estimate an exact date

20   when the proposed $750,000 annual budget would be exhausted. The Stipulation addresses those

21   concerns by requiring an updated affordability and budget analysis and by adding a one-time

 2   the EAP to serve every LIHEAP customer, but it should materially improve the resources

 3   available for program reach, benefits, outreach, or administration.



 4                   IV.     RECOMMENDED APPROVAL OF STIPULATION

 5   Q. Do you recommend Commission approval of the Stipulation terms in Section 1.12, or

 6   the EAP?

 7   A. Yes. I recommend that the Commission approve the EAP terms in Section 1.12 and approve

 8   Rate No. 89 subject to those terms. Section 1.12 improves the EAP by requiring updated

 9   affordability and budget analysis, a one-time shareholder contribution, a collaborative working

10   group, and coordination with other low-income programs. These requirements respond to the

11   concerns I raised in my Direct Testimony and provide a reasonable framework for

12   implementation and future program review.



13                                        V.     CONCLUSION

14   Q. Please summarize your overall recommendation.

15   A. I recommend that the Commission approve Section 1.12 of the Stipulation. The EAP terms

16   are reasonable because they strengthen SPS’s proposed Rate No. 89 by requiring an updated

17   affordability and budget analysis, a one-time $750,000 shareholder contribution, a collaborative

18   working group, and coordination with other low-income programs. These terms improve the

19   program’s transparency, potential reach, implementation, and future review.

20   I also support approval of the Stipulation consistent with CCAE’s position in Section 2.5.
